note: Which trailing decoration a kind of control may carry that Logic's .strings tables do not. Logic stores a bare label and the interface draws the punctuation, so a canonical spelling can legitimately differ from every corpus value by exactly this and no more. Without the table there is no mechanical answer and the question falls to a person every time, which is not a system. Each rule is witnessed: the count and example come from live AX evidence in docs/observations/evidence/, not from a convention somebody remembered.

menu_item.why: macOS draws an ellipsis on a menu item that opens a dialog rather than acting at once. Logic's tables hold the bare label.

field_label.why: a form draws the colon after a field name. The table holds the name.

default.why: A kind nobody declared may not add decoration. A button, a window title or a tab shows the label Logic ships, so a canonical differing from every corpus value by punctuation is a typo until its kind says otherwise.
